LESSON: ROTE COUNTING

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / PP2
Subject: General
Strand: THEME: OUR SCHOOL Strand Sub Strand Specific Learning Outcomes Suggested Learnin
Topic 2.1: Rote Counting
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 6

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Rote Counting, part of THEME: OUR SCHOOL Strand Sub Strand Specific Learning Outcomes Suggested Learnin in SNE  /  physical-impairment / PP2 General.

Key inquiry question: when performing singing games or rhymes. How can you count numbers 1 – 30?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. Rote count numbers 1-30 in purposive pairs/groups. Learners with speech difficulties could use alternative modes of communication to rote count numbers.

2. Collaborate with others to rote count numbers 1-30 using actions (clapping, nodding, jumping, skipping, and hopping) carefully.

3. Work with others in purposive groups/pairs to perform singing games or rhymes related to rote counting. Learners with speech difficulties could use body percussion such as hum or mime the tune

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. Rote count numbers 1-30 in purposive pairs/groups. Learners with speech difficulties could use alternative modes of communication to rote count numbers.
2. Collaborate with others to rote count numbers 1-30 using actions (clapping, nodding, jumping, skipping, and hopping) carefully.
3. Work with others in purposive groups/pairs to perform singing games or rhymes related to rote counting. Learners with speech difficulties could use body percussion such as hum or mime the tune

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Rote Counting together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
Self -efficacy: learners rote count 1-30 using actions.

Values:
Respect: learners take turns to rote count numbers 1-30 collaboratively.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Safety: learners rote count using actions carefully.

Link to Other Activity Areas:

The learner is able to relate singing songs, recite rhymes and use actions to singing games in Creative Activities.
